correctness.rationale: For every finite simple nonempty G with chi(G)=omega(G)=k, any tournament orientation of a fixed k-clique either is transitive, in which a bounded-run signed path maps to the k-level transitive tournament by maximal incoming-path height, or has a directed triangle, which reads every signed word by forward/backward traversal. Therefore each orientation of G reads all words avoiding k identical consecutive signs. Orienting G by a proper k-coloring prohibits every +^k and -^k. The canonical trailing-run DFA has one initial state, 2(k-1) run states and a sink, all 2k Myhill-Nerode-distinct; alternating run decomposition yields (1+S_k(z))/(1-S_k(z)). k=1 gives empty word only and 2 states. Formula and finite k=2,3,4 algebraic equivalence independently checked. The general proof is mathematical, not numerically certified.
